Second Derivatives of the Coefficient Hessian in the Coefficients and the Hyperparameters

Source: R/marginal_derivatives.R
penalty_d2hessian_beta.Rd

These two functions return the derivatives of penalty_dhessian_beta() that the second derivative of a marginal criterion contains. penalty_d2hessian_beta() is \(\partial^2 S/\partial\beta^2\,[v, w]\), the second derivative of the Hessian in the coefficients contracted along two directions. penalty_dhessian_beta_theta() is \(\partial^2 S/\partial\beta\,\partial\theta_m\,[v]\), the derivative of \(\partial S/\partial\beta\,[v]\) in each hyperparameter.

Usage

penalty_d2hessian_beta(pen, beta, theta, v, w, ...)

penalty_dhessian_beta_theta(pen, beta, theta, v, ...)

Arguments

pen

A penalty() object.

beta

A numeric vector of length pen@n_coef; the generics signal an error for any other length.

theta

A named list of hyperparameter values, or a named numeric vector carrying the same, checked by the generics as in penalty_dhessian().

v, w

Numeric vectors of length pen@n_coef, the directions; the generics signal an error for any other length.

...

Passed to methods. The shipped methods do not read it.

Value

penalty_d2hessian_beta() returns a square base matrix of side pen@n_coef; penalty_dhessian_beta_theta() a list of such matrices, one per hyperparameter, keyed by pen@params.

Details

Write \(S_m = \partial S/\partial\theta_m\), \(T[v] = \partial S/\partial\beta\,[v]\), and \(b_m\) and \(b_{ml}\) for the first and second derivatives of the mode in the hyperparameters. The matrix \(K_m = S_m + T[b_m]\) enters the gradient of the criterion, and its derivative in \(\theta_l\) has three parts that are present only for a penalty whose Hessian depends on the coefficients: \(T[b_{ml}]\), from penalty_dhessian_beta(); the second derivative in the coefficients along \(b_m\) and \(b_l\), from penalty_d2hessian_beta(); and the two matrices \(\partial S_m/\partial\beta\,[b_l]\) and \(\partial S_l/\partial\beta\,[b_m]\). Both of these come from penalty_dhessian_beta_theta(), the first as its component \(m\) along \(b_l\) and the second as its component \(l\) along \(b_m\), because by the symmetry of mixed partials in \(\beta\) and \(\theta\) the derivative of \(T[b_m]\) in \(\theta_l\) equals \(\partial S_l/\partial\beta\,[b_m]\). The two matrices are in general different.

The value on each branch

branch\(\partial^2 S/\partial\beta^2[v,w]\)\(\partial^2 S/\partial\beta\partial\theta_m[v]\)
quadratic, additive, structuredzerozero for every hyperparameter
separable, parent quadratic in its argumentzerozero for every hyperparameter
separable, univariate parent otherwise\(-D'\mathrm{diag}(\ell^{(yyyy)} \odot Dv \odot Dw)D\)\(-D'\mathrm{diag}(\partial_{\theta_m}\ell^{(yyy)} \odot Dv)D\)
separable, multivariate parent otherwisethe same per block, contracted by dp_contract()the same per block
a kinked parent, scad_penalty(), mcp_penalty()an erroran error

The univariate rows follow from \(\partial S/\partial\beta[v] = -D'\mathrm{diag}(\ell^{(yyy)}(D\beta) \odot Dv)D\) by differentiating \(\ell^{(yyy)}((D\beta)_j)\) once more, in \(\beta\) along \(w\) or in \(\theta_m\). The fourth response derivative is distributions7::distrib_deriv4_y(), closed form for every family that distributions7 ships and one stencil for a family defined by its density alone. The mixed one is distributions7::distrib_cross3_y(), closed form for the location families listed on its page, the Student t among them, and one central difference of the third response derivative for the other families. A multivariate parent supplies the two as arrays per block, of \(p^4\) and \(p^3\) entries, which dp_contract() contracts against the coordinates of the block in the directions; the multivariate Student t supplies both. The derivatives are taken in \(\theta\) on its own scale.

The methods of the base class and of each branch are described on penalty_d2hessian_beta.penalty().

See also

penalty_dhessian_beta() for the quantity differentiated, penalty_dhessian() for the derivative of the Hessian in the hyperparameters, beta_quadratic() for the predicate under which both are zero.

Examples

h <- heavy_penalty(n_coef = 3)
b <- c(1, -0.5, 0.3)
v <- c(0.2, 0.1, -0.4)
w <- c(-0.3, 0.5, 0.1)
th <- list(sigma = 1, nu = 4)

# The second derivative along two directions is compared with a difference
# of the first derivative along one of them.
eps <- 1e-6
D2 <- penalty_d2hessian_beta(h, b, th, v, w)
num <- (penalty_dhessian_beta(h, b + eps * w, th, v) -
        penalty_dhessian_beta(h, b - eps * w, th, v)) / (2 * eps)
max(abs(D2 - num))
#> [1] 2.504424e-11

# The movement in the degrees of freedom is compared with a central
# difference.
Dnu <- penalty_dhessian_beta_theta(h, b, th, v)$nu
num <- (penalty_dhessian_beta(h, b, list(sigma = 1, nu = 4 + eps), v) -
        penalty_dhessian_beta(h, b, list(sigma = 1, nu = 4 - eps), v)) /
  (2 * eps)
max(abs(Dnu - num))
#> [1] 7.828853e-11

# The result is zero for a quadratic penalty.
penalty_d2hessian_beta(quadratic_penalty(diag(3)), b, list(lambda = 2), v, w)
#>      [,1] [,2] [,3]
#> [1,]    0    0    0
#> [2,]    0    0    0
#> [3,]    0    0    0
